Commentary.Commentary: 280 is the target for Windies to go 1-0 up in the 3-match ODI series. They have the firepower today to chase down this total, but will this pitch support them? The last two games they have played here - they have lost batting first and second. While the one before that, they ended up chasing 309 - all 3 ODIs against Pakistan. So hard to say what we can expect in this one. Stay tuned...

Windies will feel hard done by in the last 3 overs. They had conceded only 39 runs in 7 overs of Powerplay 3 till then, with 2 wickets. But Rahim's assault on Holder deflated them. Russell and Holder started tremendously while Alzarri Joseph was inconsistent. Ashley Nurse played a pivotal role, containing Bangladesh in the middle overs while Bishoo bagged the fruit of that, picking up 2 wickets towards the end of his spell.

Now, about Tamim and Shakib. One look at the scorecard and you would feel - awww... the heroes for Bangladesh. But they nearly did the job of villains. The duo did the right thing by seeing off the new-ball bowlers but there needed to be a time when risks should have been taken, especially with 9 wickets in the bank. They left it too late and eventually, the rear part of the innings coincided with the approaching of their milestones. Tamim stayed unbeaten in the end, finishing on a wonderful 130, but any other opener would have gone past 150, having played that long.

The increasing pressure eventually got rid of Shakib who fell for 97 and was followed by Sabbir but then, in walked the pocket-sized dynamo Rahim. His cameo of 30 from 11 in a 50-run stand with Tamim lifted the tempo and that yielded 53 runs from the final 3 overs - more specifically, 43 from the last 2. That has given the bowlers some cushion to bowl at, on a slow, turning track.

A cautious 50-run stand was converted into a flourishing century partnership which continued to blossom enroute the 150-mark. But then, both batsmen were approaching their centuries and hence, perhaps slowed down. Post the 35th over, the boundaries were dried up and all of a sudden, the hosts started to work on the self-imposed pressure by the batsmen.

The start was not that great for the visiting side, with Anamul dismissed for a duck. Then the rain came which made the pitch a bit tacky - which meant that grafting was the order of the day - just 31 came in Powerplay 1. Tamim and Shakib then increased the run rate a bit and also flourished thanks to the generous Windies unit.

Okay... so eventually the tourists manage to set a target of 280. Massively competitive in these conditions. But have they lost the plot a bit in the middle overs where they carried on defensively for too long?

FOUR! Nice way to finish the innings! A short ball around off, Mahmudullah swivels and just helps it over short fine leg to the boundary! BANGLADESH FINISH ON 279/4 - THEIR BEST AGAINST WINDIES IN THE CARIBBEAN.
Mahmudullah is the new man in...

OUT! That is the end of Rahim. But what a cameo - 30 from just 11 deliveries. No time wasting. Full and around off, the keeper gets across and tries to paddle but it is a weak shot. The ball lobs towards short fine leg where Devendra Bishoo dives to his left and takes a spectacular catch. Is this the match-winning partnership? Probably worth more in gold than the Shakib-Tamim one.
FOUR! Runs are leaking. Half volley outside off, Mushfiqur slices this behind point and gets a boundary! Moves to 30 from just 10 balls with his third four.
Full on middle and leg, swung down to long on for just a single. But that brings up the 50-RUN STAND IN 18 BALLS! Tamim moves to 130 from 160 balls.
ANOTHER SIX! A touch short, Iqbal walks down the track and heaves it over mid-wicket!
SIX! A full toss to begin the over, outside off, Tamim just leans and launches it over long off! Moves to 123 from 158 with his second six and the stand moves to 43 from 16 balls!
FOUR! A boundary to end the over! 22 from it! Full on middle, Rahim backs away and slaps it straight back over the bowler for a boundary! Holder finishes with a pounding - 9-0-47-1.

SIX! Ho ho ho! Full and outside off, Mushfiqur swipes across the line and sends the ball sailing over mid-wicket! The stand is worth 33 from 14 balls! Rahim himself is on 22 from 8 balls - 2 fours, 2 sixes.
FOUR! Superb shot. Similar ball, this time Rahim gets across a touch and hammers it wide of mid off, through the covers for a boundary!

Unlucky. The batsman, that is. He shuffles around in his crease and then backs away to the leg side. Holder bowls it well outside off and MR leaves it alone. Umpire Ravi does not signal a wide. Well outside the guidelines that was.
A full toss outside off, Mushfiqur slaps hard and slices it over Chris Gayle at backward point. Alzarri Joseph comes running to his right and pushes the ball back in. Two runs taken.
SIX! SLAUGHTERED! Welcome back, mate! A length ball outside off, slower in pace, Rahim gets down on a knee and mows it over mid-wicket. The stand moves to 21 from 10 balls.
Jason Holder is back on. 8-0-25-1 so far.

FOUR! A heave-ho again. This time it is a length ball and Iqbal swings it over mid-wicket for consecutive boundaries. 10 from the over, the first double-digit over in Powerplay 3. Russell's figures read 8-0-41-0.

FOUR! Off the edge this time. A low full toss, outside off, Tamim throws his bat at it and luckily for him, the ball runs off the toe end of the bat, through the vacant slip cordon to the third man fence. Moves to 113 from 156 balls with his 10th FOUR. The stand moves to 11 from 8 balls.
Another dot. This time TI does not back away, tries playing the ball from the crease but the ball is on a yorker, moving away from him and beats tehe outside edge.
Full and wide outside off, Iqbal is backing down the leg side and hence cannot reach the ball.
On a length outside off, Rahim waits for the ball to come to him and steers it to Jason Holder at short third man for a run.
An off cutter begins the over. Tamim has a wild swipe, months early into the shot and drags it through fine leg for a single.
Andre Russell is back on. 7-0-31-0 so far.
The batsman manages only a bottom edge on that one. One run added to the total.
The batsman has driven it through mid off. They pick up a single.
WIDE. Wide down the leg side, No trouble at all for the batsman. The umpire has signalled a wide.
Full and outside off, Rahim straightaway employs the reverse sweep and gets it over short third man. By the time Jason Holder can get to the ball, two runs are taken.
Mushfiqur Rahim is the new man in.

OUT! STUMPED! Sabbir's misery ends. He has been adjudged out by the on-field umpire itself. Not even referred upstairs. Full and outside off, Rahman lunges to defend but the ball pitches and then spins away, past the outside edge. Shai Hope collects the ball and then whips off the bails. The square leg umpire raises his finger straightaway but uh oh... replays show that the foot did get dragged out of the crease - but AFTER THE BAILS WERE WHIPPED OFF. Tough luck for Sabbir. The third umpire would have saved him there, had he been referred to.
Full and on middle, Tamim comes down the track and slogs it towards long on for a single.
Full and outside off, driven back to the bowler.
The batsman has driven it through mid on. The batsmen have run through for a single. 10-0-57-2 are Alzarri Joseph's figures.

FOUR! A boundary after 64 balls! Full and outside off, Tamim reaches out and drives it behind point. The ball trickles towards the ropes and by the time the fielder from cover can get there, the ball wins the race.

DIRECT HIT WOULD HAVE HAD TAMIM. But he survives. Full and outside off, Sabbir drives it towards cover. Initially he sets off for the single and Tamim responds but then he sends his partner back. Iqbal gives it up and the fielder has a shy at the bowler's end - only to miss. They now take the overthrow.
Outside off, almost a yorker, pushed towards backward point for one more.
Outside off, squeezed through the covers for a run.

10TH ODI TON FOR TAMIM! It is the slowest century by a Bangladesh batsman in one-day cricket, informs Fazeer Mohammed on air. It has taken 146 balls. It has come through grafting and grafting on a sluggish pitch and he has eventually got there. Now, he needs to accelerate. A full ball outside off, the Prince of Chittagong just dabs it towards point and takes off for a quick single. Reaches the other end and celebrates handsomely but the job is not done. In fact, all this effort will go in waste if the visitors do not even touch 250.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single. 4 runs and a wicket from the over, Bishoo's figures read 9-0-46-1.
Full and outside off, eased through mid off for a run.
Driven through mid off by the batsman. One run added to the total.

Sabbir Rahman walks in next, at number 4, replacing Shakib. Bangladesh need boundaries. Just 21/1 in 4.2 overs of Powerplay 3 so far. Mr. Rahman averages just 17 in his last 13 games. Interesting decision to send him at this stage then...

OUT! Shakib does not get to his century! Finally a catch is taken and the 207-run stand is broken. Full and outside off, the southpaw gets down and slog sweeps it towards deep mid-wicket but has mistimed this. His casinoish luck runs out eventually and this time Shimron Hetmyer running to the ball from the deep does not make a mess. Takes the catch cleanly and the Bangla superstar departs 3 short of a ton. He seems extremely unhappy and this is now a good period for the Windies. They have applied the pressure in the last few overs and it has resulted in a wicket.
Full and around off, driven through mid on for a single.
Full and down the leg side, Tamim misses his flick and is hit on the pads. Wants the single but it is not there as the ball is just beside the keeper.
Very well bowled. Full and straight, driven straight to cover.
Full and straight, flicked to deep mid-wicket for a run.
A short ball, more pace being taken off, helped wide of short fine leg for a single.

LBW appeal but to no avail. The off cutter, pitched outside leg, Tamim looks to flick but falls over in his attempt. The ball hits his pads and then lobs. Joseph first appeals and then he goes for the catch. Cannot get to the ball but would have got to it had he taken off straightaway. Was there an inside edge? Replays seem to detect two sounds...
Very full again, flicked wide of mid-wicket for a couple.
Full and around off, driven straight down the ground through mid off for a single.
Yorker time. Alzarri time. 8-0-44-0 so far. What can he give his captain now, at the back end? A couple of wickets would not be bad...
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. One run added to the total.
ANOTHER WIDE. Too straight from Bishoo, getting one more to spin down the leg side.
And now comes the 200-RUN STAND. In 248 balls. Just the second ever for Bangladesh in all ODIs. A simple punch to long on brings up the milestone.
A touch short, Iqbal goes back and flicks it through square leg. Runs hard to come back for the second. 200 UP FOR BANGLADESH.
Helped through mid-wicket for one.
WIDE. Good turn but wrong line. Bishoo pitches this around off and then gets it to spin past Shakib's attempted flick down the leg side.
Full on middle and leg, Tamim leans and flicks it through mid-wicket for a run. Moves to 90 from 135 balls.
Short and outside off, punched through the covers for a single.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman. One run added to the total. Excellent spell from Nurse - 10-0-39-0 today.
Outside off, dabbed to third man for a run.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
The batsman has punched that ball through the off side for a single.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Full and outside off, Shakib looks to cut but misses.
Full and outside off, punched down to long off for one.
Full on middle, pushed back to the bowler.
Goes back and works it through mid-wicket for a run.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

Risky. Shakib comes down the track and looks to flick but misses. He is hit on the pads and the Windies appeal, but in vain. The batsmen take a leg bye. The hosts do not take a review probably because of the fact that Shakib was way too far down the track. Hmmm... Hawk Eye shows that it would have clipped the leg stump. It still would have stayed not out though, due to umpire's call. Yesterday, in Colombo, Dhananjaya de Silva was adjudged LBW to Keshav Maharaj in the Sri Lanka-South Africa Test and he was even further down the track than Shakib...
Pushes this towards long on for a single.
POWERPLAY 3 time. 5 fielders allowed outside the 30-yard circle. Can Bangladesh get to 300? If Shakib faces all the 60 balls, then even 350 might be possible...
Short and outside off, cut through point for a couple. What a wonderful passage of play for the visitors - 156/0 in 30 overs. In total control. With plenty of help from the opposition.
Full and outside off, driven towards long off for one.
Pain for Shakib but there is so much gain for him otherwise today. So many chances given, yet he lives on, like a cat.

Another long hop, cut in front of point for a quick single. A direct hit would have meant curtains for Shakib but he dives into his crease. Such is his luck that the direct hit does not get affected in the first place and then the bowler fumbles too. Only a piece of bruise for Shakib. Out comes the physio.
A touch short, punched down to long off for a run.
Outside off, going straight on, dabbed towards backward point.
Short and outside off, cut through point for a single.
The batsman has driven it through mid on. One run added to the total.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.

DROPPED! Another one. That casino offer might still be on for Shakib. Another piece of luck. Full and outside off, the southpaw gets down to sweep but ends up dragging it as he is far away from the ball. As a result, a top edge is induced which goes towards short fine leg. Shimron Hetmyer runs a few paces to his right and dives but the ball slips down. Two runs taken.
On middle, pushed down to long on for a run.
Short and outside off, spinning in, Shakib backs away and takes it from the line of off stump, cutting the ball through point for a single.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. The batsmen have run through for a single.
The batsman gets to the pitch of the ball and connects. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Flatter ball, outside off, driven through mid off for one more.
Full and outside off, pushed through point for a run.
Outside off, punched through point for a single.

Big appeal for LBW but the umpire is not interested. Very full ball, outside off, Shakib got a long way across to sweep but missed and was hit on the pads. Nurse appealed and even wanted a review but Holder was not too convinced. The impact always seemed to be outside the line and now, in the replays, Snickometer detects a glove.
Punches this down to long on for one more.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. They pick up a single.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. One run added to the total.
On middle and leg, played through mid-wicket for a run.

ANOTHER WIDE. Carbon copy of the previous delivery. Okay wait - my colleague whose observation is as sharp as a knife (we lovingly call him Churi), tells me that the batsman left it alone. So not exactly a carbon copy you see... caught me napping.
WIDE. Pitched around middle, spinning down the leg side, Tamim misses his flick.
Down the leg side, flicked past short fine leg for a couple.

DRINKS BREAK. 14 overs left and Bangladesh have a wonderful platform here. They can get anywhere between 90-120 which means close to 275 on an average. But can they do that? Windies will believe they can pull things back with a breakthrough. But who will deliver that? Well, Devendra Bishoo might have something to say about that. 4-0-17-0 so far.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Full and around off, Tamim lunges to block.
Short and outside off, cut through point for a run.

Full and outside off, Al Hasan gets down and tries a swipe, only to miss. The ball goes over the stumps and Shai Hope whips the bails off. No stumping appeal because as can be seen from the replays, the back foot is in.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. They pick up a single.
The Windies are wounded. They need medicine. Who better than a 'Nurse' to deliver that? 6-0-22-0 so far.
FOUR! Up and over! Are Bangladesh teeing off? Full and outside off, Shakib backs away and lofts it over mid off for a boundary! 12 from the over, Holder's figures now read 8-0-25-1.
Comes down the track and mistimes his shot over cover for a brace again.
Banged in short, pulled away through mid-wicket for a couple.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
FOUR! THE 150-RUN STAND IS UP! This keeps getting better and better for the visiting side. Down the leg side, Shakib gets across and whips it behind square leg for a boundary!
A short ball, around off, pulled straight to Chris Gayle at short mid-wicket.
FOUR! Full on middle, flicked through mid-wicket for a boundary!
Down the leg side, paddled towards short fine leg for one.
The batsman has driven it straight down the ground. One run added to the total.
Excellent yorker, well dug out.
Backs away to the leg side and on seeing that, Joseph fires it well outside off. Tamim cannot reach it and has to let it go. No wide signalled and rightly so, considering the position of Tamim.
Full on middle anad leg, flicked straight to mid-wicket.

Jason Holder is walking off the ground. He had tweaked his hamstring a few moments ago and hence, is going for a precautionary check-up, as per the on-air commentator Jeffrey Dujon. Kieran Powell is on as his substitute.
That ball has taken the inside edge of the batsman and thudded into his pads.

LUCKY AGAIN! Well, if Shakib were to play poker today, he would become a millionaire overnight. Full on middle, Al Hasan gets down to sweep but misses. Now, here is his first piece of luck on this ball. He should have been plumb LBW but such is his luck that the ball goes off his gloves and lobs towards short third man. Now here is his second piece of luck. He comes looking for the single as Tamim also responds. But then, the Prince of Chittagong changes his mind and sends him back. Shakib seems gone for all money as he slips and then tries to dive into his crease. Should have been run out. Could have been run out. But the fielder misses his shy at the striker's end. Wow. Just replace that second 'w' of that word with an 'e' for the Windies.
Comes down the track and blasts it towards cover.
Outside off, played straight to point.
A full toss, on middle, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
On a length around middle, watchfully defended.
Jason Holder is back on. He needs to do something desperately for his side, especially after a wonderful opening spell - 6-0-12-1.
A full toss, flicked through mid-wicket for one more. The stand is now worth 140 from 183 balls. But what a lovely over from the youngster.
One more yorker! Tamim loses his balance and gets the crowd to life. They cheer and applaud but then calm down once they see the batsmen take a run. The ball goes to square leg.
Magnificently bowled again. One more yorker, Al Hasan manages to dig it out again. Somehow the ball rolls to the off side and the batsmen pinch one again.
Now bowls this short, Tamim looks to pull but is hurried into it, due to Alzarri's pace and mistimes his shot towards fine leg. A run taken.
Superb ball. A pinpoint yorker, around leg, Shakib somehow digs it out towards square leg and takes a run.
On a length around off, the cutter, angling away, calmly steered to third man for a single.
A long hop, dragged through mid-wicket for one more. 6 balls, 6 singles in that over. Could have had a wicket. Should have had a wicket.
Outside off, a tap and run from Shakib to the off side. THIS IS NOW THE HIGHEST EVER STAND FOR BANGLADESH FOR ANY WICKET IN THE WEST INDIES.
On middle and leg, helped through mid-wicket for a run.
The batsman guides it to third man. They pick up a single.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for a single.

TOP EDGE, BUT WHY IS IT NOT TAKEN? Only Gayle can answer that. A short ball around middle and leg, Shakib looks to pull but the bounce gets big on him. He gets a top edge which goes in the air, somewhere not far from short mid-wicket. Chris Gayle has to jog just a few yards to his left but even then he cannot get there! Now that is a poor effort. One understands that he is not the fittest man on the ground but still... what a reprieve and that too, at this stage. A single taken.
A short ball, Iqbal pulls it ferociously and nearly spoons a catch to Chris Gayle at short mid-wicket.

FOUR! SLAP! Joseph goes short and Tamim promptly pulls it over mid-wicket. Rovman Powell gives it a good chase from deep square leg, even gets to the ball, dives and tries to parry it in but it rolls back into the ropes. The poor fielder looks at the heavens in despair.
A short ball, pulled through mid-wicket for one.
A full toss, pushed straight to cover.
Outside off, punched through the covers for a run.
On middle and leg, helped through square leg for a single.
Alzarri Joseph (5-0-26-0) replaces the part-timer Mohammed.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Plenty of width outside off, Al Hasan punches it through point for one. This is now the highest second wicket stand in all Bangladesh-Windies ODIs...

Lucky again. On a length around middle, angling away, Shakib looks to work it through the leg side but the ball sticks on the surface and hence comes late. He gets a leading edge which does not carry to cover.
Full and outside off, Tamim drives this through the covers for a run.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
On a length outside off, Shakib goes back and steers it behind point for a single. The stand is worth 120 now, from 160 balls.
Problems for Holder and he turns towards Andre Russell. 5-0-22-0 so far. Bishoo going for 17 in his 4 overs has not helped matters. The captain needs wickets.

FOUR! Ohoho! Tamim in full flow! Tossed up outside off, Iqbal dances down the track and lofts this inside out over cover for a boundary! 10 from that one and the part-timer has gone for 15 in his 2 overs.
Full and outside off, driven straight back to the bowler.
Punches it through point and gets a run.
FOUR! Lovely shot. Tossed up on middle, Shakib lofts this straight back, over the bowler's head, one bounce and into the ropes!
Outside off, driven through the covers for a single.
Full and outside off, Tamim looks to run it down to third man but misses.
FOUR! Now a half century for the former skipper. His 38th in ODIs. Short and around off, Shakib goes to the leg side, creates room and punches it behind point for a boundary!
The ball strikes the batsman very low on the pads. They pick up a single. Leg bye given by the umpire.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket. One run added to the total.

An LBW appeal but there is bat involved. Full and around middle, spinning down, Tamim lunges to flick but slips. The ball seems to have hit the pads as it goes towards fine leg and Bishoo appeals but the batsmen continue running. No signal from the umpire. A run taken.
Full and around middle, pushed back to the bowler.

HALF CENTURY FOR TAMIM NOW. He wins the race to the 50 between himself and Shakib. It is his 42nd in ODIs and daresay, he will be looking to double this. Gets there with a simple push towards long off for a single.
Full and outside off, pushed through mid off for one.
THE 100-RUN STAND COMES UP. First for Bangladesh against the Windies in the West Indies in ODIs. Brings the milestone with a gentle push down the ground for a single towards long off. Nice recovery.
Very full, driven through mid off for a run.
Full and outside off, driven through mid off for a single.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
More spin on offer. Jason Mohammed into the attack.
Down the leg side, flicked fine for a run.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.
Pushes it past the bowler towards long on for a single.
Ball hits the batsman low on the pads.
Full and outside off, driven straight to the bowler.
SIX! Up, up and away! There comes the first biggie of the game. Tossed up on middle, Tamim waltzes down the track and sends it sailing over long on!
Outside off, played straight to point.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
The batsman plays a sweep shot. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Full and outside off, Iqbal lunges and plays with an open bat face past slip to third man. A single taken.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to point.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Pushes this towards mid on.
Tossed up, eased through the covers for one more.
Full and outside off, driven through mid off for a run.
Landed around middle, Tamim looks to flick but is beaten by the ball turning in and is hit on the pads.
Tossed up around leg, Shakib goes back and gently nurdles this through mid-wicket for a single. Moves to 40 from 59 balls.
Full and outside off, chipped past the bowler towards long off for a run. Another right over from Nurse who is going at less than 3 an over in his 5th.
Short and outside off, Shakib rocks back and chops the cut straight to backward point.
Full and outside off, Tamim leans into this one and eases it through the covers for a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Outside off, watchfully left alone.
Outside off, punched off the back foot.

DRINKS BREAK. If you are thinking - 'Wow! 21 overs before the first Drinks Break!' then hold on to your horses. We have had so many overs simply because the clouds could not bear us watching and covering an uninterrupted game. There was a brief rain delay for around 15-20 minutes and hence the scorecard is showing what it is showing right now. A wonderful recovery by Shakib and Tamim after losing Anamul early. Both have played with their luck, both have been given lives and now, both are settling in nicely. The pitch is taking plenty of turn and Bangladesh might feel at home with a score of around 225 or more.
Full and around middle, pushed towards short mid-wicket.
Works this wide of mid on for a single.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
FOUR! Short and outside off, Tamim goes back and punches this through the covers for an elusive boundary.
Gets well across his stumps and then blocks it just in front.
Full on middle, pushed towards the leg side.
Devendra Bishoo comes on to bowl now.
Full and pitched outside leg, Shakib looks to sweep but misses and is hit on the pads. Shai Hope screams an LBW shout but in vain.
Short again, this time SAH gets on top of the bounce and punches it through the covers for a brace again.
EDGED, LUCKY! Short and outside off, Al Hasan looks to cut but the bounce gets big on him and takes the outside edge. Flies over Chris Gayle at first slip and the batsmen get a couple.
The batsman fails to make contact as it turned a long way.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
Full and outside off, driven through mid off for a single.
FOUR! SLAM! Alzarri sways from the line, dropping it short and a confident Shakib pulls it over mid-wicket for a boundary. 10 from that over, Joseph has gone for 26 in his 5 overs.
A short ball now, Iqbal plays that uncomfortably, with both his feet in the air and the ball hits his gloves and rolls down the leg side. A single taken.

Goes past Tamim. He is growing in confidence now. It was Tamim who started calmly and then decided to throw caution to the wind. Has been struggling a bit since. But Shakib, after playing a few risky strokes, has managed to get some runs and is playing better. Gets on top of the bounce and works it through mid-wicket for a run.
Down the leg side, Tamim walks down the track and looks to flick but the ball goes off his pads to the leg side. The batsmen pinch a quick run. Leg bye signalled.
Around off, defended from the crease.

Does not get hold of it but clears the infield. A length ball, around leg, Shakib goes through the line and heaves it wide of mid on. The wet outfield does not allow the ball to reach the ropes and the batsmen take three.

Full on middle and off, Al Hasan gets down to sweep but gets a bit of a top edge which does not carry to the man at deep square leg. After watching so many T20 games with boundaries as long as the 30-yard circle, it is nice to see long boundaries for a change...
Plenty of turn. Shakib lunges to defend but the ball pitches and then spins away past the outside edge.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
A touch short, TI punches it behind point and calls for two but then changes his mind. Settles for a single.
A bit of flight this time, Iqbal lunges and blocks.
The arm ball, on middle and leg, Shakib is hurried into his defense. Takes a quick single.
On middle and leg, helped wide of mid on for a run.

FOUR! Really nice from Shakib. Slightly short from Joseph, angling away from the left-hander, Shakib waits for the ball to come to him, gets on top of the bounce and then cuts it behind point. Moves to 23 from 42 balls with his first boundary.
Outside off, this time Iqbal waits for the ball to come to him and guides it behind point for a single.

ALMOST! Living dangerously, are these two. A length ball outside leg. Tamim looks to help it wide of mid on but the ball sticks in the pitch and he is a tad early into the shot. Ends up chipping it towards Andre Russell at mid on. Luckily for him, the ball does not carry.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
A length ball in line of the stumps, watchfully defended.
Full and straight, Tamim lunges to defend but gets a thick inside edge through mid-wicket. A run taken.
One more dot ball. Full and straight, driven back to Nurse again.
This time he tries to go inside out but finds cover.
More fuller stuff, around middle, pushed back to the bowler once more.
Full and straight, blocked back to the bowler.
On middle, helped through mid-wicket for a single.

Driven through the covers by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single. 50-RUN STAND IS UP! It has started slowly but has finally come on the 81st ball. Good recovery from the two senior men.
Comes down the track, has a wild heave and the ball goes off the inner half of the bat over mid-wicket. The wet outfield prevents the ball from reaching the ropes. Three runs taken.
A touch short now, punched through point for a run.
Full and outside off, TI lunges to defend but gets an outside edge this time, all along the ground, wide of first slip towards third man. A single taken.
On a length outside off, moving away, Tamim tries his level best to edge it behind but misses.

DROPPED! This time it is Gayle. On a length outside off, Shakib chases the ball away from his body and gets a thick outside edge. The ball flies wide of first slip where Chris Gayle flies to his left, yes, he flies, goes two-handed but only parries the ball to third man. A single taken.
The batsman has been beaten by the turn and flight on that one.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.

DROPPED! Ahh... Nurse is causing problems. He lands this just outside off, gets TI to come forward, induces the outside edge and nearly gets the wicket. But Shai Hope's left pad comes in the way. He is unable to take the catch and the ball deflects off his pads towards Chris Gayle at first slip who is taken aback. Just moves away from the line to avoid getting hit on the face and the ball rolls down to third man. Two runs taken.

Beaten again! 'Get more men near the bat!' screams an excited Athar Ali on air. Full and outside off, slightly wider than the previous one, Iqbal lunges to block but the ball spins away a long way and beats the outside edge!

BEATEN! Gets a bit of grip. Thought that might happen, partly because of the conditions, partly because of the pitch. Full an outside off, Tamim looks to defend but the ball drifts away and beats the outside edge.
Full and straight, Tamim lunges to defend but gets a bit of an edge which gets the keeper excited. The ball rolls to cover.
Time for spin. Ashley Nurse comes on to bowl. He is one of two spinners playing today. Bishoo is the other.
Just around off, watchfully pushed towards point.
Play and a miss now. On a length outside off, Shakib pushes at it but misses.
Short and wide outside off, this time Iqbal slashes hard and gets a thick outside edge to third man. Falls just short of the fielder running in. A single taken. Moves to 20 from 38 balls.
A short ball now, outside off, Tamim looks to cut but is done in by the bounce, Mistimes it to point.
Full and straight, watchfully defended.
On a length outside off, plenty of pace, steered towards third man for a single. The stand has quickly moved to 40 from 64 balls.
Outside off, slapped through point for a run.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery. One run added to the total.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman. One run added to the total.
Outside off, played straight to point.

FOUR LEG BYES! Down the leg side, Shakib looks to tuck but misses the ball. It goes off his pads and is well wide from Shai Hope. Races to the fine leg fence. Holder starts to appeal but then realizes that once the ball is pitched outside leg it cannot be given as LBW.
Around off, watchfully defended.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
Thick inside edge by the batsman, ball goes down to fine leg.

DROPPED! But a tough chance. Full and wide outside off, Tamim drives this through the covers. Ashley Nurse over there dives to his right, goes with one hand but cannot cling on. The batsmen take a single.
Outside off, left alone.
Full and straight, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.

POWERPLAY 2 has been signalled. 4 fielders allowed outside the 30-yard circle till the 40th over. Also, Alzarri Joseph is introduced into the attack. He last played an ODI on 29th September, 2017 against England.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat. That ends POWERPLAY 1 - 31/1 for Bangladesh, with 40 percent of the runs coming in one over from Russell.
Outside off, played straight to point.
Tamim follows suit now, taking another single and taking the partnership to 30 from 49 balls.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman. One run added to the total.
On middle and leg, once again, Al Hasan gets across and plays it towards mid-wicket.
Ahh... a length ball around leg stump, Shakib looks to tuck it fine but the ball hits his glove, then his body and nearly rolls down onto the stumps! Just misses the leg pole by a whisker.
FOUR! 13 from the over! Poor bowling from Russell. He threads on the pads with fine leg up and this time Tamim just tickles it past that fielder for the third boundary of the over.
The batsman was beaten and missed the line of the delivery.

FOUR! Smart batting! Fine leg was up and Tamim picked that up. He got a length ball, around middle and all he did was shuffle across and help it over that man at short fine leg. Moves to 12 from 26 balls.

FOUR! BRILLIANT! First boundary of the match. The use of the adjective is because of the lack of power in this one. No extra effort. Just caressing. Full and outside off, Tamim leans and drives it through the covers. Gets it past the fielder and earns a boundary! The stand is worth 20 from 43 balls.
A short ball now, Al Hasan looks to pull but gets a bottom edge which rolls down to square leg. A single taken. The pitch seems to be on the slower side.
Full and outside off, Shakib plays a glorious cover drive - but straight to the fielder.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Full and outside off, Iqbal drives this through the covers where Devendra Bishoo dives to his left and stops the ball.
On the pads, clipped straight to short mid-wicket.
Comes down the track now, Tamim. Signs of impatience. Cannot blame him. His side is crawling. And this is not a Test match. Tries to slap this through the off side but cannot beat cover.
A short ball, rising with the bounce, Shakib hops and pushes it wide of mid on for a single.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
A short ball, pulled behind square leg for a single.
WEATHER UPDATE - Seems bright and sunny now. Pleasant conditions to play. The only question is - for how long??? there are rain stoppages predicted throughout the game.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
WIDE. Not able to control the swing, slips this down the leg side, Shakib misses his flick.
On middle and leg, tucked through the leg side for a single.
On middle and off, watchfully defended.
On middle and leg, flicked straight to short fine leg. They think about the single but then change their minds.
A length ball outside off, SAH looks to cut but gets a bottom edge towards cover-point.
Short and outside off, Al Hasan mistimes his cut to point.
Full and straight, Shakib drives it straight back. The big man Jason gets his left foot across and stops it. Could have so easily rolled his ankle over.
Very full, swinging down, SAH misses his flick, falls over and is hit on the pads.

ALMOST A WICKET AGAIN! Shakib is flirting with his luck here. Another rolling of the fingers over the ball, Al Hasan is early onto his flick and gets a leading edge. Luckily for him, it goes wide of Holder, to his right.
WIDE. A slower ball, goes awry, is slipped down the leg side, Shakib lets it go.
Full and down the leg side, Tamim clips it through mid-wicket for a single.

NEARLY DRAGS IT ON! Russell almost strikes immediately after the break. Full and outside off, Shakib, who seems to be in no mood to leave balls alone outside off, throws his bat at it. No footwork and that results in an inside edge. Luckily for him, the ball hits his pads and rolls past leg stump. Russell starts to celebrate but then realizes what has happened.
A short ball, pulled straight to short mid-wicket.
We're back! All of a sudden, the rain disappeared, everything got cleared and the players are back on the field.

So let us do a small summary of the innings. Were Bangladesh right in batting first? Maybe the overhead conditions tricked them into doing so. When the captains came for the toss, it seemed bright and sunny but then it got overcast. Many a times, batsmen get out mainly due to the fact that they are expecting rain around the corner and that exactly has consumed Anamul. If this does end up being a start-stop game, Mashrafe might wish that the toss happens again. Stay tuned...

This was coming... the drizzle was getting heavier by the minute and the umpires have called for the covers. Only the two right now as it seems to be a passing shower. And indeed, the clouds seem to have been blown away with just a small portion of grey left. There are plenty of blue skies visible but just as I type that, an additional cover is brought in. Fingers crossed.

Ahhh... a testing short ball, SAH goes for the pull but the ball gets high on him and goes off the top half of the blade. Luckily for him, the ball eludes the man at square leg and by the time fine leg can get to it, two runs are taken.
Short and outside off, Al Hasan cuts it hard but once again, cannot get past the barrier named Lewis at point.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
Short and outside off, cut through point where Evin Lewis dives to his right and stops the ball.
One more leave outside off.
Outside off, coming in, left alone.

Excellent from Lewis! That is one good thing with this 'new' Windies side.  Fielding. They have remarkably improved and this is a testament to that. Outside off, Shakib plays this through point and seems to have found the gap. But Evin Lewis throws himself to his left from backward point and stops it cleanly. Then immediately has a shy at the striker's end but misses. Tamim was in though.
Outside off, driven straight to mid off.
Full and outside off, Shakib leans into this one and drives it through the covers for a couple.
It is raining, it is raining, it is raining...
Outside off, Shakib feels for this one and gets beaten.
Outside off, finally one is left alone.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
They are getting ready... they are waiting... oh dear.. it may pour any moment. Heavy rain is sweeping across the Atlantic Ocean, says Fazeer.
On middle and leg, tucked through the leg side for a couple.
Overdoing the short stuff, Iqbal sways away from the line.
A sharp bouncer, around middle, Tamim ducks.
On middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
Outside off, punched towards cover.
On a length outside off, punched through the covers for a single.
Full and straight, Shakib times it beautifully, uppishly but wide of Holder, down the ground. Mid off covers it up. Al Hasan wants the single but is sent back.
Shakib Al Hasan walks in at number 3, replacing Anamul.

OUT! This time Anamul fishes and is caught! Early success for Holder. So easy for him, isn't it? He is just fresh from a 11-wicket haul in the second Test and has already struck with his third ball. Similar line to the previous delivery. Full and outside off, not too wide but not too close. A teaser is the word. Anamul left the ball previously but this time he goes after it. Looks to defend but the hint of away movement takes the edge. Straight to Ashley Nurse at second slip. Classical outswinger from Holder, just taking it away and inducing the mistake.
Tempting line, full and wide outside off, swinging away, watchfully left alone.
On a length outside off, Anamul looks to defend but the ball kicks off a length and takes the batsman by surprise. He is in no man's land and gets hit on the thighs off the gloves.
Jason Holder to bowl with the second new ball.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover. A decent start from Russell on international comeback.
WIDE. Slips this down the  leg side, TI misses his flick.
A short ball, around middle, Iqbal sways out of the way.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full and just around off, awkwardly defended down the pitch.
That is a beauty. Russell pitches it right up to the batsman who looks to defend but then gets it to move away. Tamim is totally squared up.
On a length around middle, tucked towards square leg.

The dark clouds come nearer and nearer as the conditions get more and more overcast. The wind has picked up too. Cannot help but think that a shower is about to come. The players are already in the middle. Andre Russell will bowl first up with the first new ball. Tamim Iqbal to face. Anamul Haque is his partner. Here we go!

Andre Russell is having a chat with Fazeer Mohammed. Admits that there is a little bit of anxiety coming into this game owing to the big gap but he is excited all the same. States that T20s are totally different from ODIs and that is the main reason for his anxiety as he has not played too much of List A cricket of late. Praises his unit for qualifying for the World Cup in the Qualifiers in Zimbabwe. Is excited, like the others, to see Chris Gayle playing and hopes he sets the stage on fire. Is hopeful of maintaining their dominance by using the experience of the seniors in this Windies side. Says that he has only one state of mind - to be positive and has started thinking more about the game. On the youngsters, he says that there is nothing much to worry as most of them are already exposed to the game.

Windies captain, Jason Holder, is not too perturbed and says that he was not too sure what to do first as the last time they played here, it became a good pitch to bat on in the second innings. Hopes to use the early morning moisture and take some quick wickets upfront. Admits that the 2019 World Cup is in their minds but for now, their main concentration is to win this series. Is happy that the 'superstars' are back - namely Andre Russell and Chris Gayle.

Mashrafe Mortaza, the one-day skipper, admits that it was tough for Bangladesh in the Test matches but ODIs are a different format and hopes that they put a good total today. Cites the reason as their success during the 2007 ODI World Cup, where they batted first in the Caribbean and defended totals successfully. Informs that there have been plenty of changes from the Test side - with a mixture of youth and experience.
TOSS TIME! Tails is the call and it is a Tail. BANGLADESH WILL BAT FIRST.

PITCH REPORT - Jeffrey Dujon doing the report says that the pitch looks so dry that there are some very significant cracks in it already. The surface is solid though. The ball should come onto the bat but the bounce should be moderate. Because of the sheen on top of the track, the spinners will not get too much of turn, he says. Win the toss and bat first, opines Dujon.

WEATHER - Did I say blown away in the Tests? May be. For now, we hope that a huge swarm of dark clouds get 'blown away' as in a matter of 15 minutes, it has gone from being nice, warm and sunny to being overcast. Hopefully, we get an uninterrupted game.

One of the gorgeous venues in South America welcomes us to the first ODI between Windies and Bangladesh. Nothing much to talk about the Tests as far as Bangladesh are concerned as they were blown away. Hopefully, we get some sort of a contest in the ODIs and T20Is. Hello and a warm welcome!
